text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Versa 3 Health & Fitness Smartwatch with GPS, 24/7 Heart Rate, Alexa Built-in, 6+ Days Battery, Black/Black, One Size (S & L Bands Included) Now that I have used this Fitbit for a few weeks I feel like I have an idea about it. I've wanted a Fitbit for years, I've heard nothing but amazing things about it and how great they are. Well, to be honest, I am not seeing the greatness of them now that I actually have one. Maybe it's because this is the newest one, maybe there are still bugs to fix, and maybe it could be my phone that just hates everything about the Fitbit app. Honestly, I don't know but either way, I am so unimpressed with this Fitbit.

The pros I have found out is that it was easy to set up and make an account with Fitbit. Everything downloaded, updated, and whatever else perfectly. It was easy to change all the settings and personalize everything the way I wanted it. I love that you can customize the face so that it matches your personality or the types of apps or stuff you want it to show first right on the face. I like that you can control your music and pay for your watch too. Those are great ideas and honestly if I got out more and whatever else I can see where tons of people would totally get so much use out of it.

My biggest beef I have with this though is the fact that I wear it constantly and I want to keep up mainly with my steps, how much I move, and my sleeping patterns. It doesn't have any problems keeping up with all of that and so much more. The problem I have with this watch is the fact that it disconnects from the wifi and then becomes difficult to sync to the app, if at all. I've already had to reset to factory settings once to get it to reconnect to the app, which also has its own set of challenges because once the watch goes the app doesn't want to do much either. I can't remove the watch to re-add it in the app and I'm unable to view the wifi connections to change them or re-add them. It's like everything stops and becomes completely unusable. It's a real pain, to say the least.

Being completely honest, the watch I replaced with this Fitbit was way better and I never had any issues with it syncing to my phone, the app, or anything else. It did everything that this one does but just not as pretty, which honestly I'd much rather the watch to work and do what I want it to do than to have the cool face and whatever else.

I am so unimpressed and honestly bummed about this watch not living up to the hype. I am hoping that everything works out and the bugs are fixed soon if these are bugs, but I've no idea. Right now the watch is acting up again and honestly, I am thinking I am about to have to reset it again. If this happens I am going back to my old one that I know works just fine. Honestly, don't waste your money on this one just yet but wait to see if the bugs are fixed in a few months.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Versa 3 Health & Fitness Smartwatch with GPS, 24/7 Heart Rate, Alexa Built-in, 6+ Days Battery, Black/Black, One Size (S & L Bands Included)

text_fidelity_a: GREAT WORKING TOOLS Bike Hoist for Garage Ceiling Mount Pulley System Bike Storage, 55 Lbs Limit, Set Of 2 Bike Hangers for Garage Storage In a typical two car garage, like mine, you really don't have room for much more than your cars. With them on the floor, we were constantly having to move them, just to get to other things like the lawn mower, etc. This two pack of Great Working Tools bike hoists solved the problem. Note: if you're not accustomed to doing this kind of installation, you might want to hire a handy man. But, this is in my 'wheel house'. The trick is to make sure you attach the hangers in ceiling joists. If the joists are not in a workable location, fasten some 1X6 cross members to the ceiling, between the joists. Then, mount the hangers to those members. Using the lift is simple. place the hooks under the seat and handle bars, hoist it up and tie it off to the included cleat. The whole set up is very well designed and made, with quality materials. Good purchase. Five stars.

I will say that I disagree with the description calling it a "larger" size sleep mask. It definitely is not that.  When I got the package in the mail, I opened the mask and thought this is way too small for me. BUT, I soon realized that while average in size, this sleep mask is really amazing! Items included come in increments of x1 (bandaids = x5) So, if traveling in a group for more then a day.. I’d suggest a larger kit or, at the very least supplement this one.. However, there are reviews on here saying these are a “high quality product.” These are good quality for the price point. But for this price obviously the frame is plastic, lenses are basic triacetate & can scratch easily, polarization film is on the outside of the lens which can degrade and are not very impact resistant.
Compare that to higher quality sunglasses (typically above $100) the lens material is likely to be polycarbonate. The polarized film is sandwiched between two layers of polycarbonate meaning the polarized film can never wear out and provides impact protection. That’s the big difference.
I like these glasses for just a basic pair to use for activities where I’m afraid to use my nicer sunglasses. Are these worth the price? Mansader 6 Person Family Camping Tent,Waterproof Windproof with Top Rainfly,Easy Set Up,Pop Up Tent for Outdoor Camping Hiking Travel The two of us are seventy-something, live in Georgia (which is very hot and humid), and all the windows in our rental house are painted shut. In a sustained blackout, we would probably die. After the "What did our grandparents do when they didn't have air conditioning" discussion, I decided that having a few well-ventilated pop-up tent "bedrooms" outside would mimic the breezy screened sleeping porches of old, pre-air conditioning in the South.

We have separate bedrooms, so I wanted two tents for our comfort and also so there's plenty of room for the dogs who insist on sleeping with one or the other of us. Fortunately, we do have a few shady areas in our back yard where we can pitch our tent rooms. And if we have to evacuate, we can throw our tents into the back of our truck along with our camping mats, solar oven, solar generator/panels, and our kelly kettle.

Of the two tents I got, this 6-person one is larger and more durable but a little bit harder to set up; the other one is one of those that you can essentially toss in the air to unfold, then stake down. This one is going to be mine, because I'm the one the dogs want to spend the night with. Robert gets the other one because he's older with spine issues and a little less capable of putting up a tent than I am. I like that this tent fits neatly into a zippable carry bag and has everything included. We aren't likely to use it for camping, but it's a real relief to me to know we have it for our emergency "blackout kit" in case we need it.
text_fidelity_b: Mansader 6 Person Family Camping Tent,Waterproof Windproof with Top Rainfly,Easy Set Up,Pop Up Tent for Outdoor Camping Hiking Travel

text_fidelity_a:
Century Original Wavemaster Freestanding Heavy Punching Bag I filled this with water and am not very impressed with it's stability. I'm 5'9" and around 200# and can throw a decent set of punches and round houses. I expected it to lean some, but only a few punches, even mid-power, causes the whole thing to dance around. I had it on carpet, then put it on a foam pad on the carpet. Nothing kept it from moving around. My son (9 yo) can get a bunch more punches it without it moving too much, but it still moves. I see other reviews say to use sand, so I might go that route.
It appears the seal for the cap does not keep the base water tight. After a short while, water is escaping and dribbling down the sides. It's not a huge deal, but unexpected.
The top portion does have a natural lean to it - it's not straight up. I don't have an opinion on that yet.
All the bad out of the way, it is relatively easy to adjust the height, even my son was able to bring it from a setting well over his head down. It's also a lot of fun to hit and is a good workout.
text_fidelity_b: Century Original Wavemaster Freestanding Heavy Punching Bag

TiTo High Strength Titanium Alloy Tent Stakes Tent pegs Nail pegs for Canopy Camping Tent Dia 8mm and Length 240mm only 56G (8x300mm) These are the beefiest, most heavy duty titanium tent stakes I've ever seen. It is kind of overkill, making these out of titanium when a good chromoly steel of the same weight would be nearly as good. I'm sure a company could make quality steel stakes (albeit a little thinner) that would be just as strong, but I'm digressing, when you go premium, go big, go really big! And these are that.

Unfortunately the listing is kind of messed up and ambiguous. When I received them, as I hoped these are the stakes that are 8mm in diameter and 300mm in length. They are also around 70 grams a piece, not the lighter weight which my understanding is for a shorter version. I was anticipating the extra weight since another reviewer gave meaningful and helpful feedback. I completely understand and agree with the criticisms expressed about the heavy weight and the high cost. I also don't think these are good for backpacking, possibly could work for staking down heavier things like EzUps or large canopies. These are SOLID and reflect that fact with heavy weight. I don't mind that they weigh a lot because I only plan to use two of these stakes for setting up a secure ridgeline across poles, with lighter weight stakes for the guylines.

The cordage loops at the end seem kind of cheap and low quality in comparison to the stakes themselves. The stake materials, welds and finishing all look great, although a couple stakes new-out-of-the-package have a slight curve/bend to them. There are no sharp edges or other apparent issues. Overall I'm very pleased.
text_fidelity_b: TiTo High Strength Titanium Alloy Tent Stakes Tent pegs Nail pegs for Canopy Camping Tent Dia 8mm and Length 240mm only 56G (8x300mm)

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Evanston Screened Camping Tent, 6/8 Person Weatherproof Tent with Roomy Interior Includes Rainfly, Carry Bag, Easy Setup and Screened-in Porch (WARNING- This is a long review. I am covering areas about this tent that were a concern to me. If you want a summary, go to the paragraph titled THE BOTTOM LINE)

I wanted to take the time to review this tent. I spent a LOT of hours researching, watching EVERY video and reading every available review I could find out there about this tent to decide which I would get. It was between this tent and [[ASIN:B001TSCF96 Coleman Montana 8-Person Tent]]. As it turned out, we had an immediate need for TWO tents, so I got both of them. You can see my review of the [[ASIN:B001TSCF96 Coleman Montana 8-Person Tent]] by clicking the link

WHAT IS THIS TENT LIKE?
One of the things I was concerned about was the thinness of material. We live in a very high elevation and get constant breezes or wind. There were a number of reviews that spoke of their tents snapping or ripping after only a gentle breeze. The fabric is thin, yes. But it does hold up.

Enough people have posted photos, so I won't post one as of yet. The best way to secure this tent is to ALWAYS leave the fly on. An unexpected storm or wind can come up at any time, and I personally feel that the tent is much more stable with the fly on than without. Make sure that you always stake down everything, including ALL of the ropes. That is what keeps the tent stable and secure.

FLOOR
The floor is very nice, and if you use a tarp underneath and take off shoes before entering, it will last quite a while. I also recommend not using chairs with small pointed feet on it either- it will wear out the floor quickly.

WINDOWS
The windows are perfect. They are protected from all but the most severe of rainstorms so you can leave them open if you like. The back window is open at all times, yes, but if staked down, it is not that big of a deal. If we plan to take this on crowded camp sites, I will sew two rings at either back seam and attach a thin fabric when changing. No big deal.

POCKETS AND LANTERN RING
The pockets are nice and in a good space. There is also a ring for hanging a lantern on if you like.

HEIGHT
The height is perfect for us- the tallest is 5 ft 9 inches. Taller people might not like this tent. The screened in porch is a bit narrow for those with long legs. You pretty much need a chair to use it unless you are a kid and don't need to lean back.

SCREENED IN PORCH
I LOVE this thing. I really do. This is my happy place. It is perfect for two camp chairs to look out at night or in the day. The door of the tent can stay open adding to a spacious feel. It does get wet in the rain. I am currently designing a fly to go over the porch and roll up into the tent when not in use. So far I am almost done with the one half of the fly and plan to finish the other half this week if I can. I hope to do that before the tent is taken down.

Without a fly, your stuff will get wet. There is an area that you can sweep the water into when wet, I use a sponge mop to clean it up so it will dry faster. Otherwise it puddles and does take a long time to dry.

POLES
The poles went up well for us, but you just have to take your time when putting up the tent. Do not race through the process, the fabric can rip if you don't.

TENT SPACE
Our biggest concern was ACTUAL usable space for us. We found that putting a queen inflatable double height mattress in there (Coleman) we have plenty of room for two of us. If using an additional single mattress, we can still do it, but it works best with a sleeping bag on the floor and picked up at night if a third person is in there (child).

When using or covering up the porch in rain, the porch makes a great extension for activities, talking, or just sitting and enjoying the view (if not raining). I absolutely love the design of this tent.

LIGHTING
The tent color is half of the beauty of this tent. The light bright colors are cheerful, let in a lot of light, and also keep it from feeling gloomy on rainy days. At night you can see through it, so keep that in mind when you are getting ready at night.

DOES THIS STAY UP IN STORMS?
The big question. I have an answer for you. We purchased this tent the week before Labor Day (US). We put the tent up immediately and treated it with silicone spray. We didn't need to- it is already made from silicone impregnated ripstop nylon. The seams also came pre-treated with silicone on the fly. AMAZING!.

We have had this tent up with daily use since then and it is now October 8,2016. So far it has been through extreme heat, breezes, high winds, thunder storms, all night rains, and heavy rain storms. The tent has stayed up with no observable damage at this point and stayed very dry too.

IMPORTANT POINTS
After reading MANY reviews on this tent, I decided to help it stay up, I would reinforce different areas. Anywhere that there is a plastic hook, I put a piece of garden twist tie into the fabric loop that holds the hook and tied it around the pole to help it absorb any shock of high winds. Any other plastic rings or hooks were reinforced in the same way. I tucked the ends of the twist tie way under so no chance of the fabric blowing into sharp edges and tearing in high winds.

STAKES
I also recommend getting other stakes for the tent. They stay in the ground during storms more easily too. I got [[ASIN:B01IEBKK92 Pack of 16, 7075 Aluminum Outdoors Tent Stakes & Rubber Hammer & Guyline Tensioner with Reflective Pull Cords & Carrying Pouch]] to use in the fly staking process, and used the ones that came with the tent for the actual tent staked to the ground.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Honestly, this is my favorite tent of all time. It is my happy place. I absolutely LOVE the design, set up, colors, and ventilation of this tent. With a mattress, it is still private to lay down with the windows open and you can still look out at the sky and enjoy the scenery. When you are in the tent and want to have breeze, the front door open makes it seem so airy and wonderful. I can not rave about this tent enough. Five weeks of constant use is more than we planned for, but it has held up so far.

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED at five stars.

QUESTIONS AND UPDATES
If you have any questions I have not answered, by all means ask. I hope I can be helpful, as I know how it helps me when others do the same. I will update with any more input should I have anything else to share or if there are problems with the tent.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Evanston Screened Camping Tent, 6/8 Person Weatherproof Tent with Roomy Interior Includes Rainfly, Carry Bag, Easy Setup and Screened-in Porch

text_fidelity_a:
Gymnic / 10" Softgym, Assorted Colors (One of Pink, Blue or Yellow) I received this mini ball as a gift, and I have been using it for fitness, mainly with the workout [[ASIN:B004HF74DU Tracey Mallett-Pilates Super Sculpt]]. I also purchased a similar ball, [[ASIN:B00374O8JK 9" Body Back Ball & Pump]], so I will be comparing the two balls in this review.

The Overball that I have looks like the blue one pictured above. Although you can't quite see this in the photo, the surface of the ball is covered with slightly raised dots; this improves the ball's gripping surface, making it easy for the Overball to stay in place under your back, behind your knee, etc. The Overball comes with a small, short plastic straw to inflate it and a small plastic pin to use once the ball is inflated. The ball fills up easily enough with the straw; I found that the inflation process took only a minute or so. The problem I had was when I went to insert the pin. The Overball does not retain air very well at all, so every time I tried to insert the pin, the ball deflated almost completely in the brief moments it took me to get the pin in place. I had to repeat the process several times; finally, I inflated the Overball way beyond the point where I wanted it to be, put the pin in as quickly as I could, and was satisfied with the results. I did not have this same problem when inflating my Body Back Ball (which comes with its own nice little hand pump); that ball definitely seemed to hold the air better to allow for pin placement.

In terms of actual performance, I have had no problems with the Overball. It does seem a little squishier than my Body Back Ball, but that might be because of the inflation issues--if you are looking for a firm ball, this is definitely NOT the right choice! But for use with Pilates and other core workouts, where a slightly deflated ball is desirable, the Overball works quite well, and I would recommend it overall.
text_fidelity_b: Gymnic / 10" Softgym, Assorted Colors (One of Pink, Blue or Yellow)

This is pretty good, actually. Mounting the base was tricky - or more, finding a place to mount the base, it isn't quite as versatile as a spring clip, but after I had it in place it kept the tube just where it should be. The magnet is strong enough that it draws the tube in if you get the position relatively right, and it keeps it there pretty much without exception.

JumpSport Heavy Duty Durable Trampoline Anchor Safety and Stability Kit Set Includes 4 Screws and Straps for High Winds A great product. Last winter we lost a much beloved trampoline to extreme winds. I set out on a search for a product that could prevent the loss of the replacement trampoline. I found a number of products on various websites that could best be described as variations on a tent stake design. They offered stakes that were straight or U shaped, and I was very nervous that in a windy situation (especially with rain softened ground), that the stakes would just pull free. I was about to fashion my own solution using spiral dog stakes when I found this kit.

Suffice it to say that the components are sturdy and well made. They are packaged well, and the instructions are clear and easy to follow. However, what makes this a five star product is that it contains everything you need to create a stable tie down for a trampoline, and it contains enough anchors to tie it down for wind from any direction. The anchors are not trivial to "screw" into the ground. I did it on a day after heavy rains and still required a tool for leverage. This was reassuring, because it meant that they would hold fast when the ground dried, and would allow the straps to transfer load from the trampoline frame to the stakes and the ground effectively.

I was very pleased with the product, and would heartily recommend it.

UPDATE: This stakedown kit works very well. Since installing, we have had four windstorms with gusts over 20 mph, and the trampoline has stayed perfectly in place. Highly recommended.
text_fidelity_b: JumpSport Heavy Duty Durable Trampoline Anchor Safety and Stability Kit Set Includes 4 Screws and Straps for High Winds

text_fidelity_a:
Swagman XTC2 Hitch Mount Bike Rack I'll try to get to the details not already mentioned multiple times:

FOLDED DIMENSIONS: 38"H x 15.5"D x 10"W when completely folded with the hitch bar removed. I was really pleased to see what a small footprint this takes up when not attached to the car. Folding takes about 40 seconds, and removing the hitch bar - if desired - takes another 60 or so and requires an allen wrench. I made a partially-sided box out of scrap wood to hold and protect this nicely behind the car in the garage when not in use.

When folded, the center bar and two side bars come to within about 1/8" of each other without touching - very nicely designed.

TIGHTENING MECHANISMS: I was delighted to see that the mechanisms to hand tighten the wheel holders are the high quality, non-abrasive clamping type, rather than the screw-down-a-machine-screw type that flakes paint and distorts metal over time.

CONSTRUCTION: All immovable joints are welded, the rubber straps on the wheel holders are very thick, and the ratcheting clamps are fantastic. The anti-wobble hitch pin works, but you'll need to carry your 19mm socket/wrench if you want to remove this at your cycling site (but it's quick and easy to fold and throw in the trunk).

LOCKING: It's been mentioned before over several reviews, but to consolidate points: One small lock will fit through the hitch pin nicely, but you need larger locks to keep the center arms from being removable. One reviewer enlarged his with a drill to make his next size larger lock fit, but I won't do the same to mine for fear of removing the finish, possibly making a weak point for rust to form. Locking the arms with the correct size lock is a great feature and a great selling point (actually, that was what finally got me to pick this one over the similar model by Hollywood Racks), but it would have been absolutely fantastic if the hitch pin and arm clamps took the same size lock so you could get a matching set that uses one key. Alternatively, I would have gladly paid a couple bucks more to have appropriate locks included.

Absolutely recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Swagman XTC2 Hitch Mount Bike Rack

TFO Air Camping Sleeping Pad 1lb Ultralight, Upgraded 40D Tear-Resistant Nylon, Textured Inflatable Camping Mat with Compact Carrying Bag for Backpacking/Hiking The Earth is the world's largest heat sink & everyone who has slept on the ground knows that the earth will suck all the heat from your body as you try to sleep. This mat rolls up very compact, fills quickly & breaks down quickly. It is superior in every way to the pool float a lot of people (myself included) use.

This mat uses dozens of little chambers instead one big one which makes it fill faster & breaks down easier. The fill valve does not have a protrusion like a straw or a nipple, rather I kind of had to "kiss" it to blow it up. I was able to blow it up in about 65 seconds (I timed it). The port has a check valve that works very well so the air stays inside the mattress. The valve flaps around a bit & makes a squeaking sound that my wife compared to a Wookie.

To deflate, the valve opens to a 1" diameter hole. Because of the multiple air chambers, air does not get trapped in the rolled end when rolling it up. This makes a huge difference because it can be folded before all of the air is out. It took me 2 minutes to deflate, roll & bag the mat. Of course this is in my living room & not in 2-person tent.

I confess that I haven't slept on this mat yet but I did lay & roll around on it. It is just as noisy as my Thermarest mat and feels about the same thickness. It's not uncomfortable but also not particularly supple. It is on par for this type of low-profile, inflatable mat.

I usually tent-camp off my motorcycle where weight isn't so important but space is. This mat is way more compact than any of my other mats. If I was tent camping from the car I would probably stick with my self-inflating mat but this will definitely go on my next motorcycle trip. It is very light, probably light enough for hiking or biking but I can't speak to that.
text_fidelity_b: TFO Air Camping Sleeping Pad 1lb Ultralight, Upgraded 40D Tear-Resistant Nylon, Textured Inflatable Camping Mat with Compact Carrying Bag for Backpacking/Hiking

-Seems and looks solid for those worried about appearance.

Cons:
-May need to fiddle with how many spacers to use with each bolt. There are six bolts on each rack.
-Installation, certainly the first time, might take up to 20 minutes for each rack. And sometimes it's hard to get those big wingnuts to thread properly given the awkward angle since the bolt is vertical and you may not have much space to install the wingnut between bolt and roof of car.
-Very easy to have the spacers fall off the bolts before wingnut is threaded. I had two or three roll off the back of our vehicle. No biggie on a flat concrete driveway but can be a problem on gravel or camping.
-It doesn't lock, which is okay for our needs. I can probably run a cable lock through the frame/tires and part of our roof rack. This may not keep the racks from being stolen but it would be a real pain to remove with bikes mounted. -Of course, it's nice to leave the rack on all summer if you use it frequently, but note someone can get a rack off in 3 minutes if there's no bike on it.
-For any roof rack, it may take a little strength and height to put the bike on top of a car/SUV and simultaneously align that front fork with the locking axle (built into the rack). I'm over 6 feet but my wife is 5'-6" - no way can she use this rack w/ her hybrid. Might be different w/ an ultra-light tourer and a foot stool.
text_fidelity_b: Alloy Car Roof Bike Bicycle Fork Mount Carrier Rack Max Load 44 lbs

King Koil Twin Air Mattress with Built-in Pump - Double High Elevated Raised Airbed for Guests with Comfortable Top Inflatable Bed with 1-Year Guarantee from The Manufacturer This mattress looked great out of the box. Now less than ten days later it's on its way to the garbage bin.

It looked good at first. The material seemed high-quality and the built-in pump worked great to inflate it, relatively quickly. I went online while the mattress was inflating and read all of the manufacturer's suggestions, including the one to inflate it and let it sit overnight before use to "stretch out", then add more air. I followed all the instructions carefully.

Just a few hours after fully inflating the mattress and without anyone using it or even sitting on it, I pressed on it with my hand and noticed it was already mushy and not nearly as firm as when first inflated, so I topped the air off again and let it sit overnight without using it. The next morning it was mushy again, but I figured maybe this was the "stretching" the manufacturer was talking about. That night I inflated the mattress to full firmness, made up the bed, and went to sleep. About three hours later I woke up with the hard floor under me and a tangle of deflated air mattress wrapped around me.

So clearly, the mattress was defective and had arrived with a leak. Well, that happens. It was really unfortunate because I had no other bed at the time to use, but I had gotten a cheerful email from the manufacturer here on Amazon right after I ordered, telling me if I had any problems to contact them and they would be sure to honor that warranty twhich hey make such a big deal of offering, and make things right.

I emailed them to let them know that right out of the box the mattress was leaking air badly. They replied with the same instructions I found online, saying it was probably "stretching out" and I just needed to top the air off. I replied that I had now spent two nights on the mattress, and the only way to use it was to set an alarm to wake up every two-and-a-half hours to reinflate it before it went completely flat. I asked them to please do as they said and work with me to make it right.

That more than a week and three emails ago. I have emailed them over and over (the only way to reach them.) The manufacturer simply stopped responding after the first email. They did not provide any customer support, no advice, nothing. They did nothing at all to honor the warranty they offer. I tried finding a patch kit on my own for this thing, but I can't even find the leak, it seems to be in the sealing of one of the seams. It's basically garbage at this point, because it's useless. The photo is of it sitting waiting to go out with the trash less than two weeks after being bought.

If you look at the one and two star reviews, many people have had the same issue. With this mattress, it seems like either you are one of the lucky ones and it works perfectly out of the box, or it just doesn't hold air at all and you are screwed, because the manufacturer is not going to keep their word and honor that reassuring-sounding warranty that they offer to entice people into buying their expensive air mattress.

So, if you need a bed and want to roll the dice, try your luck. I did, and I certainly regret believing the untrustworthy, dishonorable shysters who manufacture the King Koil.

$150 dollars, straight out into the trash.
text_fidelity_b: King Koil Twin Air Mattress with Built-in Pump - Double High Elevated Raised Airbed for Guests with Comfortable Top Inflatable Bed with 1-Year Guarantee from The Manufacturer

Cons: The base is flimsy. Mine sags downward in the middle with the helmet sitting on it. It's made of two pieces of 1/8" black acrylic. My solution is to remove the stick-on rubber feet and mount the whole base on a piece of 3/4" oiled walnut, like genuine deluxe display cases have, or a piece of quarter inch acrylic.

Prorack Kayak Carrier My only previous experience carrying kayaks has been tying them to the top of a rental car with old patch cords through the windows. So my comments here might not be wise, but hopefully a fresh perspective.

First thing I noticed is that you have to have the cross bars installed on your roof rack, not just the bars that run perpendicular to your windshield.

I really like the idea and design on the four "pads" that you lock down, they flex in (or out) to conform somewhat to the bottom of your vessel. They give you confidence that the pressure you apply is working with you and not against you (not that you're applying too much).

They lock on fairly easily with a simple bolt and sort of a wing-nut type add-on. This could be slightly better. You have to pull that wing-nut add-on back to encase the head of the bolt, which is intuitive and not difficult, but the system reminds me of a tool for cutting lock holes in doors that I broke the first day. An all metal specialty-bolt would inspire much more confidence.

The straps they give you are just okay. They work, but they're not the heavy duty ratcheting straps you might be imagining. Similarly the ropes and hooks they give you to tie down the front and the back are less impressive than some specialty-cut bungee cords with rubber-covered hooks on one end and quick attachment mechanism on the other that you might wish for.

I don't have a high opinion of the general public, and thus I remove all such equipment from my car, even when it is possible to lock it in place. Locks are always appreciated, though, although half the time they are just "best effort" on these types of devices anyway. Even so, they're fairly quick to remove and replace, especially if you can mark or remember the exact placement.

In summary, this is a good (and apparently unique, from reading other reviews) idea, and the bulk of the product seems to be of high quality. A few bucks extra spent on higher quality accessories would kick this up to a premium product.

Ultimate Body Press Wall Mounted Doorway Pull Up Bar Wow, what a monster! This ULTIMATE BODY PRESS WALL-MOUNTED DOORWAY PULL UP BAR is a serious piece of exercise equipment--the bar measures 4 inches around. This allows a solid, comfortable, non-tiring grip for large hands. A heavy duty pull up bar like this one is an excellent choice if you have limited space for exercise equipment--you can use it for resistance band exercises as well as for pull ups.

But the bar does require a fair amount of space (an over door space about 38 inches wide). You mount the bar on the solid "king studs" located about 3 inches on each side of most interior doorways. Thus you will need a doorway that allows you to reach those studs. Some of my condo's doorways are set flush against an interior wall on one side, and are totally unsuitable for mounting this bar.

Also, you need ceilings that are high enough to allow you some headroom for pull ups. My condo has 8 foot ceilings, and most of the doorways leave 15 inches above the opening. This is enough room, but just barely. If you use the bar for resistance band training, you need adequate space to move around in front of the doorway, too.

The installation hardware (lag bolts and washers) is included. However, you will need some tools in order to install the bar--an electronic stud finder, a level, a power drill, a 5/16" drill bit, a socket drive adapter for the power drill (optional but recommended), a 17mm socket wrench, and a 17mm open socket wrench. The sheet of installation instructions (in English) is extremely clear and easy to follow.
text_fidelity_b: Ultimate Body Press Wall Mounted Doorway Pull Up Bar

JOOLA Ben Johns Hyperion CFS Pickleball Paddle - Carbon Surface with High Grit & Spin, Elongated Handle, USAPA Approved 2022 Ben Johns Paddle So this is Ben Johns' new paddle after switching over from Franklin. I really like this paddle.

The first things that stick out to me are grit on the paddle face and the nice grip.

The face of this paddle is carbon fiber, unlike the fiberglass face on his previous paddle. Carbon fiber is more durable and allows for more spin than fiberglass. The grit on the face is immediately apparent when you touch it--it might be the grittiest paddle I've felt. I've noticed that I can actually get some extra spin if I use my wrist more when hitting the ball (which I probably shouldn't be doing).

Another aspect I really like is the grip. The grip is not completely flat like most grips, but has a nice texture to it. It absorbs sweat well and it's held up pretty well over the few weeks I've been using it so far.

Overall, this is a fantastic paddle designed by the world's best player. If you can stomach the premium price (or are a high-level player), get this!

We purchased this stove for emergency preparedness and for camping without using propane or camping fuel. Based on the reviews for this product on Amazon we purchased it.

We tried it out at our scout meeting to see if the Campfire & 2 pot set held up to the hype. We had no trouble lighting the fire with a piece of pine lighter with some small twigs off the ground.

After feeding the fire a little at a time we started the boiling process with 20 ounces of water in one of the pots. There is a small opening on the cooking ring to allow for more wood to be added during cooking. Small amount of smoke when the fire was first ignited, less than a few minutes the fire was almost smokeless as the fire was consuming the wood efficiently.

It took a little less than five minutes to boil the water and only left small ashes after the fire was out. Clean up on the stove and pot set was simple water and dish soap. On the bottom of the pot some soot was still stuck on, but after using a magic eraser it quickly looked like new.

I did have one defect in the product as a spot weld on the cooking ring wasn’t made and was loose. After contacting the company they quickly sent out a replacement cooking ring to replace the loose ring. Customer service was a pleasure to deal with and seem to have a passion for taking care of their customers.

Positives:
+Minimal fuel (wood) usage to achieve cooking heat
+Opening to allow for more fuel to be added while cooking
+Green way to camp
+No fuel canisters to throw away
+Great customer service
+Easy to operate and clean
+Great size for campouts for a large family
+Campfire exceeded expectations
+Comes with storage bag
+Lifetime guarantee on workmanship

Negatives:
-If dry wood is not available may take longer to ignite and have more smoke output

Overall, I am very impressed with the Solo Stove Campfire & 2 Pot Set and the customer service to back it up.

text_fidelity_a:
JJ JUJIN Wood Burning Camp Stove Portable Backpacking Stove Folding Stainless Steel Grill with Carry Bag, Perfect for Outdoor Camping Hiking Picnic BBQ Cooking 8 Inch I love this stove design. I really do. The problem is that the way it is made, I have yet to be able to use it.

HOW THIS COMES
This has a great case with a zipper on it. That protects the stove and keeps it handy to transport it while camping.

WHAT IS THE PROBLEM?
This is a camp stove. That means that it does not have to have a mirror finish. For some weird reason, the company that made this stove, found it necessary to cover every single stove part with blue plastic sticky protector sheet. The problem is that they put all of the parts together and the paper won't come out of a lot of overlapping areas such as hinges and bent edges.

THE BLUE WON'T COME OUT
I have tried and tried to get all of the plastic off of this stove so I could use it. Unfortunately, even though I was using tweezers and pliers I can not get the plastic out from the hinges. If this was not a stove for BURNING things, it might not be such an issue. Unfortunately, I can not get the plastic out totally. I refuse to burn this until all of the plastic is out. All together, I have spent a few days on this combined.

THE BOTTOM LINE
It takes a really long time to get the plastic pieces out of this unit. Even after a few days I am still trying to remove the plastic. I am not sure it will all ever come out. I refuse to burn this with plastic in it since there will be food made with it.

MY RATING
TWO STARS. This stove could be a five star stove. With this plastic problem, I am very frustrated with it and wish I had not gotten it. If the company could put it together and leave the plastic off of the hinge and attached areas, at least you could peel it off and have not issues with it. As a camp stove, I am not interested in having a mirror finish at the expense of hours of work to remove plastic.

PHOTOS
I have posted quite a few photos of this stove after I first got it and then around the first set of hinges I could not remove the plastic from. When I can spare the time, I try to remove more plastic, but this is taking a really long time with way too much effort.
text_fidelity_b: JJ JUJIN Wood Burning Camp Stove Portable Backpacking Stove Folding Stainless Steel Grill with Carry Bag, Perfect for Outdoor Camping Hiking Picnic BBQ Cooking 8 Inch

WOD Nation Knee Sleeves for Weightlifting (1 Pair) Premium Support & Compression - Powerlifting & Weight Lifting - 5mm Neoprene Sleeve for The Best Squats - Fits Both Women & Men Let's start with the sleeves:

I am a wedding photographer with two bad knees and I needed a pair of sleeves that could provide good support and be comfortable simultaneously. After reading many reviews, I eventually bought these because of the ranking and many reviews.
The sleeves fitted tight with very good compression over my knee, but at the both ends they were so uncomfortable. There is a lot of pressure in both ends that were biting my skin and would left a considerable mark after I took them off after a while. But I got used to it after a 15 minutes.
Therefore I gave them a test (actually twice in two days). I used them outdoors for around four hours with very mild activity (walking sitting, going indoors, etc.), in a day that was warm but not hot or humid. When I took them off after I came back, they almost burnt backs of my knees, because they trapped all the sweat and they were entirely wet on that area. And my knees were itching for an hour too! So they didn't leave me any other choice rather than calling the customer service to use their 100% satisfaction money back guarantee. Here is what happened then:

I messaged the customer service, and the only respond I received was that "Amazon handles our returns, and you just go there and return the items". Ok, if you are an Amazon user you know that Amazon accepts returns on almost anything this way, it is not satisfaction guarantee. So I returned the used pairs (means you have to pack them again, print the label and drop them off if you are not satisfied). I would never use those pairs anyways, but just saying this is not satisfaction guarantee. I am sure that the returned pairs should go to trash can when they receive them. Satisfaction guarantee means you are not satisfied: money back! Just sayin'.

All in all, I ordered two of "Ultra Flex Athletics Knee Compression Sleeve"s , and they were just the perfect match. They are kind of fabric and they breathe and are super comfortable even for long uses like mine.
